newsitem.title: GERMANY: Harsh winter lifts '96 German electricity demand.
newsitem.headline: Harsh winter lifts '96 German electricity demand.

text.p: The harsh German winter in 1996 led to a 1.9 percent increase in electricity consumption to 466 billion kilowatt hours, the representative body for the German electricity generating industry, VDEW, said on Friday.
Total electricity sales in 1996 were 126 billion marks, up from 125 billion marks in 1995, the VDEW said. At the same time, the number of employees in the sector fell five percent to 178,000.

Heinz Klinger, president of the VDEW, said that milder temperatures in 1997 had stymied the rising trend, and said that energy consumption in the first quarter fell 3.3 percent to 122 billion kilowatt hours.
According to the VDEW's calculations, energy consumption levels were around half a percent lower than average economic growth since 1991 and this trend was continuing.
